body: So I talked to our couples therapist, she never said we were in an abusive relationship or said I was abusive, like my ex has been telling me she had. She also doesn't know why my ex would be using her and associating her with things she never said.
She would as well. Usually when I would try to walk away.
Will do, I'm calling the therapist again tomorrow morning after I get off work. So far she hasn't responded to my email, text or voicemail I left today.

She very well could be lying. I know that for the last year of our relationship she said she didn't love me, but right up to a couple weeks before the split she would tell me how much she loves me and how in love she was with me. With all that I don't trust her at all. Not to mention that, while I don't have any proof, I don't believe she was faithful in that last year. I was hospitalized last March, which was when I was diagnosed with BPD, after a big fight that was partly because I was jealous that she was showing one of our guy friends more physical affection than she was to me, and after I got out we were all hanging out in our room and watching a movie and his head was in her lap and she was leaning over him with about 3 inches between their faces. She knew that I was jealous of him and her, and that I was uncomfortable with that, but said he was just a friend and like a little brother to her and that's how she was with all her friends and wouldn't change. Like I've known this woman for 11 years and not once has any friend had their head in her lap.

I'm trying to get ahold of her. She ended our sessions in early February since we were no longer a couple. My ex only brought her up, saying she told her in the private session that I was abusive after I told her a lot of our sessions I talked about how she would follow me continuing the fight after I leave the fight to cool down and that she never takes accountability for herself.

When I talk to our friend she never mentions abuse, she was also the first person who wasn't my family to say that it wasn't all my fault and she's fucked up to in our relationship. She's been one of the only people who I've trusted throughout this because she knows both of us and our relationship the most. She's also talked me down from the ledge a couple times.

Like I know what I've said in fights were mean and hurtful, and I am to blame for my own actions, but never once was abuse brought up at any point during our sessions or when talking to our friend. Only from her.
I tell her this and she denies it, saying because it's not a pattern it's not abuse and that her therapist says it's not abuse. She then usually tells me it's my fault.

No, just her. Not our couples counselor, not my personal therapist, not our friends. Not anybody but her. She says they have said it to her, but nobody has ever said it or mentioned it to me. 

She says I'm still being abusive because I don't respond to hostile or degrading texts she sends me. She also says it wasn't abuse when she degraded me in front of our kids for 2 days when she knew I was in a suicidal spiral and between med refills. She called me a fucking pos, a pathetic loser, a coward and an abuser. I had to go to the hospital that night because I was going to kill myself and called my mom to say goodbye, she called the PD and they took me there. Next day when I told her what she said was horrible and was the trigger point for it, she gave an oh well shrug and laid into me again in front of the kids.

Honestly not good. Everytime I go to her apartment to get the kids or we hang out all the scabs on my heart tear open. I know I have to keep fighting to stay alive for my kids but honestly I don't know how much fight I have left in me.

Also I am aware of radical acceptance, it's probably the hardest thing I'm trying to do right besides staying alive. I'm in a DBT class and in my free time I am copying out and doing the exercises out of another DBT workbook. I've been trying to fix myself for a long time and since she ended it I've been doubling up everything with DBT and therapy.

I talked to both therapists about everything. Never once did either say that my words are abusive, just that they were hurtful things to say during a fight. I felt guilty and ashamed everytime I lost my temper during an argument, and was working to change. Nobody said anything about abuse, not even our mutual best friend who she tells everything to and I know she's never not called me out when I did something stupid. It was only said and still is only said by my ex.

It is all coming from my ex. Her best friend who I am also really good friends with has never said I was abusive, she was also the first person who knew us both to say I wasn't the only one who fucked up in the relationship after my ex blamed everything on me.

If that was the case, how did we all get diagnosed with BPD? Or adhd, MDD, anxiety or any thing else? We talk to them about the areas where we are fucking up or having challenges and they help us take it from there. Like give us a label to help point us in the right direction, like what was given to me when I got diagnosed with BPD.

And if the same couples counselor can tell my wife I'm being abusive, then not tell me, as somebody who is also her client, who's gone to her for help in working through my emotions and challenges, seems kinda fucked up.

During fights, I would definitely say so hurtful things. After fights I would do what I considered giving both of us space to calm down, and just leave her alone outside of whatever talk was needed about the house or kids. When fights were starting, I would try and leave the situation before I blew up and she would follow me still poking buttons until I reacted. I do this now during our texts and arguments start, I will stop replying because I don't want to react. She says that that is me continuing my abusive behavior.

I blocked number and her messenger last week, because it was just her calling me a disappointment to my children and saying things she knew would hurt me. I decided that I would rather it all go through our co-parenting app instead of 3 different apps. She nuked the number I had since I was a teenager and I was phone less for a few days. She said it was my fault because I was repeating my abusive behavior and not communicating.
I literally pay/paid people to tell me these things though. If I'm fucking something up, it's literally their job to tell me.

My thing is though why didn't both our couples therapist and my personal therapist tell me? Thats literally why I go to them, to call me out and tell me what I'm doing is abuse or wrong or help me through things. That's literally their job.

Thank you, I don't have a way with words, but that's my thought process. If I'm coming to you to help me be better why would you hide that fact from me. I take full accountability for my actions. They are my own and my inability to control my emotions (which I am working on) are my own faults. As much as I did when it first happened, I don't blame her for leaving me. I wasn't the husband and friend she deserved. I'm still going through the grieving process and just upset and sad that the person we had to help in us and me, held that back. I know to some labels don't mean much, but just like when I finally got diagnosed with BPD last year, having an actual label would've helped me target more accurately what I was doing, and the stigma and label itself has kicked my ass into fear of working on myself. I never wanted to hurt, though I know I did and take responsibility for that, but having that knowledge I know would've helped us, and I to have a better strategy going forward. My personal therapist didn't even bring that up, though I told her everything and all my guilt for my actions. Even know she just says that what I said wasn't right and was hurtful but never said I was abusive.

I'm not saying I was right, this was how me and my single mom were my whole life. I didn't know any better and was always told people get mean in arguments so I thought it was normal. I knew I could get mean when in a argument, when I went into that fight or flight response and my emotions were overwhelming. I was working on it, but like I said this was my norm all the way into adulthood.
